transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2025-10-07 15:00 PT
Duration: 55 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Samir (Redwood AE), Elena (Redwood SE), Iris (Redwood CSM); Dr. Priya Kapoor, Theo Marsh, Anya Feldman, Luis Ortega (Meridian)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be rough):
Meridian is scoping a 6-week POC to evaluate Redwood for inference on genomics/clinical NLP workloads. Key decision factors: security (PII handling, SOC2/hipaa style controls), predictable throughput for batch analysis and interactive queries, and unit-cost at scale. Team wants clear success criteria (latency p95, throughput, cost per million tokens), a benchmark plan using a 72-hour sample trace, and deployment decision guidance (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private).

Topics:
- Success criteria and decision gates for the POC
- Workload sizing and request distribution
- Benchmark metrics and methodology
- Timeline and roles
- Security/compliance constraints influencing deployment mode

Action items (captured briefly here; see metadata list): Samir to share pricing, Elena to run bench, customer to share traces & docs.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Samir Patel: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. Quick intro — I'm Samir, AE on the Redwood inference team, Elena is our systems SE who will run the benchmarks, and Iris is our CSM. Priya, Theo, thanks for joining — wanna do quick intros on your side?
[00:18] Dr. Priya Kapoor: Yeah hi, Priya here, VP Eng at Meridian. We run a platform that does genomics and clinical note normalization — sensitive PII, heavy token sizes, mix of batch and interactive flows.
[00:32] Theo Marsh: Theo, cloud arch. We're evaluating options to replace our homegrown GPU fleet for inference; main drivers are latency SLAs for interactive and predictable costs for nightly batch workloads.
[00:45] Anya Feldman: Anya, security, focusing on encryption, access controls, and regulatory scope.
[00:55] Luis Ortega: Luis, ML platform. I'll help gather traces and run the pilot infra-side.
[01:04] Elena Ruiz: Great — quick agenda for the hour: align success criteria, talk workload shape and throughput, propose benchmark plan and the decision criteria for deployment modes, and map timeline. Sound good?
[01:16] Priya: Yep, go ahead.

[01:20] Samir: To start — can you describe the two primary workloads? We heard interactive clinical query and nightly batch — any additional complexities like long context, streaming, or tool-calls?
[01:33] Theo: The interactive queries are typically 1-2k tokens, sometimes up to 5k when we include patient history. Batch runs are large: a nightly job that re-annotates ~120k records, average 600 tokens per record but has big tail. We also do CSV-style reranking for some prioritization flows.
[01:50] Elena: Got it. Any hard p95 latency targets for the interactive side?
[01:55] Priya: Ideally sub-1s p50 and under 2s p95 for typical queries — but we'll accept higher p95 if we can get predictable throughput for batch. The business cares more about interactive latency for the clinician UI.
[02:08] Samir: Good. And concurrency for interactive?
[02:10] Theo: At peak we see ~60 concurrent sessions, average 25 sustained during clinic hours. Batch runs we want to finish within a 3 hour window overnight.
[02:21] Elena: Helpful — that gives both latency and throughput targets. For the POC, we usually set explicit success criteria like: 1) p95 interactive <2s on chosen model, 2) nightly batch completes inside 3 hours with no more than X GPU-hours, 3) end-to-end cost per 1M tokens below a threshold, and 4) security checklist satisfied. Does that match your internal decision gates?
[02:46] Priya: Yes — add model output quality: we need no more than 1.5% regression on a curated prompt set compared to our current baseline. We'll send that eval suite.
[02:56] Samir: Perfect — we'll run quality reg tests tied to each benchmark.

[03:05] Elena: Ok next — deployment modes. Quick rundown: Hosted (Redwood-managed multi-tenant endpoints) gives fastest time-to-value, streaming & function calling support, and no infra to manage. Dedicated is reserved GPU pools with tenancy isolation and capacity guarantees (good for predictable throughput and lower unit cost at scale). Private is a VPC or on-prem package where you run inference in your network — best for strict data residency and max control.
[03:31] Theo: From cost perspective, we care about predictable unit cost for nightly batch. From security perspective, we might need Private for regulated datasets. But Private is heavier to stand up — we want to understand the tradeoffs.
[03:45] Anya: Our SOC2/hipaa-like constraints require customer-managed key management (HSM/KMS) for certain PHI workflows and a full audit trail. If Hosted can't satisfy that for those workflows, we need Private or at least Dedicated in a VPC with KMS integration.
[04:02] Samir: Totally — we support KMS integrations in Dedicated and Private; Hosted has Bring Your Own Key options in some cases but we'll need to map your exact policy. We can map out a hybrid approach: host non-PII inference on Hosted and put PHI flows in Dedicated/Private. That's common.
[04:19] Priya: Hybrid could work — need to quantify the complexity and cost.

[04:25] Elena: On benchmarks — we propose the following plan: you provide a 72-hour sample trace (anonymized where needed) capturing token distribution, payload sizes, and concurrency. Redwood will run: 1) a latency sweep on Hosted for 2 candidate models (one smaller quantized option + one higher-quality), collecting p50/p95/p99 and token/sec; 2) a batch throughput run to simulate nightly jobs and measure GPU-hours and cost; 3) a cache/continuous batching test to see cost savings for prefix-heavy requests. We'll append quality regression evals against your suite.
[04:54] Theo: For the batch sim, how do you model things like KV cache and long-context rollouts? Our batch jobs sometimes re-use contexts across records.
[05:05] Elena: We'll include KV cache settings and simulate realistic prefix reuse. Also test quantized model variants to measure impact on latency and cost. We can provide a micro-benchmark harness that you can run on-prem if you want to reproduce results.
[05:18] Luis: If we do Hosted first, how do we measure warm-start vs cold-start effect? Our clinicians are sensitive to intermittent cold latencies.
[05:26] Elena: We'll run both steady-state and cold-start stress tests — look at p99/cold-starts and also measure tail latencies with simulated autoscaling scenarios. We'll capture the distribution and produce a report with recommendations (batch window sizing, batching config, cache hit rates).
[05:40] Priya: Ok noted. On timelines — we're targeting a vendor decision within 8 weeks. Doable?
[05:47] Samir: For a 6-week POC we can do Hosted bench and quality eval in week 1-3, Prod-like Dedicated sizing and cost projection in week 3-5, and security deep-dive for Private in parallel so you have materials for decision by week 6. That hits your 8-week procurement window with buffer.
[06:05] Anya: For Private we'll need network diagrams and requirements — can Redwood provide an onboarding checklist for Private install?
[06:12] Samir: Yes — we'll share the Private deployment checklist and the VPC peering/egress requirements. Action: Samir to share those docs in the next 3 business days.
[06:21] Theo: What about SLA and fallbacks? If Dedicated zone is saturated during a major batch, do we have automatic fallback to Hosted or lower-tier models?
[06:31] Elena: We support routing policies — you can configure fallbacks to Hosted variants or cheaper models. For POC we'll document expected behavior and run a failover simulation to validate correctness.
[06:42] Priya: Pricing — can you ballpark unit costs for Hosted vs Dedicated? Need something to show finance.
[06:49] Samir: We'll share a spreadsheet with a few scenarios: low-concurrency interactive cost for Hosted, cost per GPU-hour for Dedicated (with reserved vs burst options), and an estimate for Private deployment support costs. The spreadsheet will include token-based examples to map to your 72-hour trace.
[07:03] Anya: Also need to know about log retention and audit trails — requirement is 7 years for certain audit events. Does Redwood retain logs that long or do we push them to our SIEM?
[07:14] Iris Kwan: We don't retain raw content for that long on Hosted by default; for Dedicated/Private you can configure long-term retention or forward audit logs to your SIEM. We'll get you the specifics on audit event types and retention options.
[07:27] Priya: Good. On model control — we sometimes want to pin quantized weights and custom tokenizers. Which modes allow that?
[07:35] Elena: Private gives the most control (you can run your own builds). Dedicated allows model pinning and curated variants; Hosted offers curated model catalog with Redwood-managed updates. For very custom tokenizer changes Private is safest.
[07:47] Theo: For benchmarking, can you simulate our concurrency pattern? We have spikes to 60 concurrent sessions but low average.
[07:55] Elena: Yes — supply a concurrency trace and we'll replay it. We'll include spikes and the autoscale response curve to measure tail latency.
[08:03] Luis: We worry about data exfiltration risk. Does Redwood support row-level encryption or tokenization before it hits the model?
[08:11] Samir: We support pre-tokenization and client-side tokenization patterns; we can also integrate with customer-side tokenization to strip PHI before sending to Hosted if needed. Private eliminates egress concerns altogether.
[08:24] Priya: Let's define measurable success criteria on this call so procurement has clear gates.
[08:29] Samir: Agreed. Proposal for POC success criteria (we'll put in writing):
- Functional: quality regression <= 1.5% on customer eval set
- Latency: interactive p95 <= 2s on chosen model under expected concurrency
- Throughput: nightly batch completes within 3 hours using <= X GPU-hours (we'll compute X from your trace)
- Cost: demonstrable unit cost per 1M tokens within your finance tolerance (TBD)
- Security: required controls (KMS/HSM, SSO/SAML, audit logs) documented and validated
- Operational: runbook for failover and SLA expectations provided
[09:05] Priya: That looks good — finance will set the cost tolerance; we'll get back to you.
[09:10] Samir: Next, benchmarks specifics — we'll run two model candidates: Candidate A (quantized 8-bit) and Candidate B (higher-quality 16-bit). For Candidate A we'll measure cost per token improvements and latency. For Candidate B we'll focus on quality vs latency tradeoffs.
[09:26] Elena: We'll include quantization delta reports — quality vs token reduction. We'll also test batching window sizes to measure throughput vs latency tradeoff.
[09:34] Anya: For the security deep-dive, I want to involve your infra lead — can we get an hours estimate for Private install?
[09:41] Samir: We'll include a rough SOW estimate in the doc — typical Private installs vary but we'll include a ballpark (people hours, infra prerequisites).
[09:49] Theo: Any specific networking constraints for Private?
[09:52] Elena: We ask for access to a subnet with outbound to Redwood control plane (or an air-gapped option with periodic bundle exchange for strictly offline installs). We'll send the checklist.
[10:03] Luis: During the POC, will Redwood be able to run benchmarks that mirror our cost model — e.g., preemptible GPU usage vs reserved commitments?
[10:12] Elena: We'll model both reserved and spot-like savings when estimating Dedicated costs. For Hosted we can show typical multi-tenant unit economics.
[10:20] Priya: Ok, at a high level this looks doable. Let's get the trace and the eval suite over to Elena. Who should I send it to?
[10:27] Samir: Send it to elena@redwood.ai and cc samir@redwood.ai; Iris will help with onboarding and scheduling.
[10:33] Iris: I'll set up the follow-ups and calendar invites; we'll schedule the private feasibility call after we get Anya's requirements.
[10:40] Priya: Anything else?
[10:42] Samir: One more — we'll include a mock SLO table in the deliverable mapping p50/p95/p99 to cost buckets and recommend routing policies.
[10:50] Anya: Great. Please include audit event examples in the security docs.
[10:54] Samir: Will do.

Recap & explicit next steps (live):
[10:58] Samir: Recap — Customer provides 72hr trace + eval suite + security doc (Theo/Anya/Luis). Redwood provides pricing spreadsheet, Private checklist, benchmarking harness and report. We'll aim to finish the hosted bench and quality eval in two weeks, dedicated sizing and cost projection by week 4-5, and security deep-dive by week 3-6.
[11:18] Priya: That works. We'll try to get the trace by 10/09.
[11:22] Samir: Great — action items captured. Thanks everyone.

End of meeting.

Notes on transcription quality: a few proper nouns (model names, tokenizer) may be slightly off; timestamps approximate.
